title: How to Color Grade a SaaS Product Demo Without CapCut: The Full Workflow
summary: A screen-and-camera SaaS demo, from recording to a graded, shared link, without exporting to CapCut: record, cut, zoom, grade the camera and screen separately, and share with analytics, compared step by step with the CapCut route.
body_markdown:
To color grade a SaaS product demo without CapCut, grade it in the tool you record and share it from. In Tella, the camera and screen are separate tracks, so under **Style → Filters** you put **Warm** or a LUT on the **Camera** and **Crisp** or **None** on the **Screen** . The grade covers every clip, and the share link plays it immediately. There's no export, re-import, or re-upload.


[How to color grade your webcam without CapCut or Premiere](https://www.tella.com/blog/color-grade-webcam-without-capcut-or-premiere) covers the webcam on its own. This post is the whole demo: record, cut, zoom, grade, and share.


## The CapCut route, and where it adds steps


People reach for CapCut because it's free and has good filters. For a hosted SaaS demo, the route looks like this:


1. Record screen and camera in a screen recorder.
2. Export the recording and import it into CapCut.
3. Cut, add zooms, and add filters or a LUT.
4. Export again.
5. Upload to a video host or YouTube, and paste the link.
6. For any change after sharing, repeat steps 3 to 5 and replace the link.


Two things hurt most. If your recorder saves camera and screen as one composited file, the camera bubble and your UI get the same grade unless you mask the bubble. And the link people have already opened doesn't update.


## The Tella route


1. **Record** screen and camera with the Mac app, Windows app, Chrome extension, or web recorder.
2. **Cut** mistakes, silences, and filler words.
3. **Zoom** on your clicks and lay out screen and camera.
4. **Grade** the camera and screen separately.
5. **Share** the link, which already includes every edit.


Change anything later and the same link updates.

## Step 1: Record with separate tracks


Record the demo in Tella. The camera, screen, and mic are saved as separate tracks, which is what makes a camera-only grade possible later. Record in your usual lighting and don't fix color while recording; it's easier to change later than to undo.


## Step 2: Cut first


Open the video in the[editor](https://www.tella.com/editor) and use[Auto Cut](https://www.tella.com/auto-cut) to remove silences, filler words, and mistakes, or edit the transcript. Cut before anything else, because zooms and layouts are timed to what's left.


## Step 3: Zoom and lay out


Open **Effect** and click **Generate zooms** to add zooms from your clicks, then adjust any you don't like. Use **Layout** to arrange screen and camera, or[Auto Layouts](https://www.tella.com/auto-layouts) to generate layout changes. For the camera frame, a circle keeps attention on the product;[Blob](https://www.tella.com/blog/blob-camera-for-product-demos) or Pop-out gives the presenter more presence.


## Step 4: Grade the camera and screen separately


Press` B` for **Style** . Under **Filters** :


**Camera tab:** start with **Warm** , which corrects the blue cast of most webcams under office lighting. For a film look, click **Customize** and choose a LUT (the built-in **Portra** at around half intensity suits most faces), or upload your own` .cube` file.


**Screen tab:** use **Crisp** , which adds contrast and a little saturation without shifting hues, or leave it at **None** . Avoid Warm, Cool, Mono, Fade, and LUTs on the screen: they change your UI's brand colors, and people who use the product will notice.


The filter applies to every matching clip. For a clip recorded at a different time of day, check **Apply to this clip** and correct it on its own.[Color filters for product demos](https://www.tella.com/blog/color-filters-for-product-demos) goes through every preset.


## Step 5: Check, then share


Play the video once with Filters open. Look at skin in the brightest and darkest moments, and at small text on screen. Then click **Share** : the link, embed, and[analytics](https://www.tella.com/video-analytics) are ready, and an MP4 export in up to 4K includes the same grade.


If you tweak the grade next week, the link updates, and nobody needs a new one.


## When CapCut is still the right tool


- **Short social cuts** with trending templates, effects, and stickers.
- **Heavily stylized edits** with masks and keyframed effects.
- **Footage you didn't record** as separate camera and screen files, where you need masks to grade the bubble.


For those, export from Tella and finish in CapCut. For a demo you share by link and update over time, keeping it in one place saves a round trip every time. See[Tella vs CapCut](https://www.tella.com/alternatives/capcut) .
